highlights_headline: The next SkiaSharp release improves rendering reliability and updates Apple and Uno platform requirements.
highlights_body: Changes include display-paced Android texture rendering, Linux HarfBuzz coexistence fixes, corrected native callbacks, and stricter text-input validation. Apple applications and Uno consumers should review the migration requirements below.

breaking.title: Raise Apple deployment targets
breaking.body: SkiaSharp and HarfBuzzSharp native libraries now require macOS 12 and iOS, tvOS, and Mac Catalyst 15. Raise application deployment targets accordingly, retaining any higher framework requirements. Managed minima are aligned with these floors; the earlier macOS 11 and iOS/tvOS/Catalyst 14 native baselines are superseded. The updates support Xcode 27 builds while preserving .NET 9 targets.

breaking.title: Move Uno applications to Uno Platform 7
breaking.body: The non-Windows Uno views now require Uno 7 and .NET 10. Legacy platform runtime packages are retired. Migrate legacy WasmShell builds to the .NET SDK WebAssembly pipeline. SKSwapChainPanel now derives from Grid, uses a CPU raster fallback, and returns a null GRContext on non-Windows Uno targets; use SKCanvasElement for GPU rendering. Remove uses of RaiseOnUnsupported. The Windows App SDK facade retains its ANGLE-backed control.

breaking.title: Rebuild custom WebAssembly archives for WebGPU
breaking.body: WebGPU C++ support is now compiled into libSkiaSharp.a rather than on the application link line, avoiding C++ flags being applied to C sources. Consumers newer than .NET 8 must use rebuilt archives containing that support; older or GPU-disabled custom archives do not satisfy the link contract. JavaScript glue remains a consumer-side link input, and the .NET 8 built-in WebGPU path is retained.

breaking.title: Replace the retired fork-specific WinRT target
breaking.body: The native fork-specific WinRT target is retired. Move builds that depended on it to a supported Windows target. Desktop Windows, WinUI/Windows App SDK, and NanoServer remain supported; this retirement does not remove those targets.

breaking.title: Supply valid encoded text-buffer lengths
breaking.body: Font text operations now reject negative byte lengths with ArgumentOutOfRangeException and odd GlyphID byte counts with ArgumentException before native calls. Pass nonnegative lengths and complete 16-bit glyph IDs to BreakText, glyph conversion, counting, measurement, and text-path operations. Empty and well-formed inputs retain their behavior. Encoded BreakText results count bytes; string and char-span results count UTF-16 code units.

breaking.title: Use a single encoding unit for character-code conversion
breaking.body: StringUtilities.GetUnicodeCharacterCode now validates encoded byte width rather than UTF-16 string length. Supply one ASCII character for Utf8, one BMP character for Utf16, or one Unicode code point for Utf32. Use Utf32 for supplementary characters; multi-character and multi-unit inputs are rejected rather than partially decoded.

bullets.lead: More robust SkSL and region processing
bullets.detail: Same-milestone Skia m156 updates reject shader slot-count overflows and invalid runtime-effect types, prevent undersized conic-region buffers, and stop partially constructed runtime-shader pipelines from executing.

Graphite preserves cap and join bounds for hairline and subpixel strokes and compares complete paint keys. Ganesh GL no longer uses a BGRA8-as-RGBx upload configuration that is invalid in GLES; readback is unchanged.

Automatic continuous GLTextureView rendering, including MAUI SKGLView.HasRenderLoop, follows display callbacks instead of unthrottled buffer swaps. Drawing stays on the GL worker; explicit render requests and lifecycle progress remain independent of display pacing.

Bundled HarfBuzz functions bind locally on Linux, preventing internal calls from being redirected to an incompatible system HarfBuzz loaded by GTK. Exported entry points and managed signatures remain unchanged.

Skia callbacks use one-byte native boolean values, and HarfBuzz callbacks use four-byte hb_bool_t values, while public managed signatures retain bool. This corrects callback interoperability, including Apple ARM64 interpreter returns and false-returning HarfBuzz font callbacks.
StringUtilities.GetString now reports ArgumentNullException for null byte arrays instead of NullReferenceException. FromCString fixes a native buffer over-read and writes directly to SKData.

The OpenGL module backing cached WGL pointers is retained, optional stream callbacks and XPS COM ownership are corrected, and browser capability handling is fixed. A separate fix addresses front-buffered stream retention.

bullets.lead: Less allocation during copying and text processing
bullets.detail: Valid managed image pixel copies avoid an intermediate SKData allocation while preserving native validation for invalid inputs. HarfBuzzSharp AddUtf32 string calls avoid per-call encoded arrays, and feature-string formatting uses bounded stack storage without changing decoding.

Windows libraries move to Windows App SDK 1.7.250909003, and WinUI's bundled ANGLE advances to chromium/8118. ANGLE symbols are packaged with matching DLL names. These updates do not change declared Windows runtime minima.
